To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
respiratory neuron activity is determined by synaptic inputs, and that these synaptic connections can explain some, but not all, of the activity patterns of respiratory neurons.
phrenic activity is driven by medullary premotor neurons that are inhibited by expiratory neurons in the Bötzinger Complex, which also inhibit themselves.

phrenic activity is determined by the balance between excitatory input from medullary premotor neurons and inhibitory input from Bötzinger neurons, and that this balance is determined by reciprocal inhibition between the premotor and Bötzinger respiratory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional synaptic connections that determine the patterns of activity of respiratory neurons and the role of these connections in generating the respiratory rhythm.
the synaptic interactions among neurons of the respiratory network that produce its activity patterns.
the functional synaptic connections between respiratory neurons that produce the patterns of activity that control the timing of breathing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network of respiratory neurons in the adult rat brainstem has been studied in great detail and that the functional interconnections among them have been determined for many of them.
we are still a long way from understanding the respiratory network, even though it is a small and relatively accessible network.
the respiratory network of the adult decerebrate rat is still not completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the respiratory network is not a static structure.
respiratory rhythmogenesis in the adult rat is not a simple, well-understood process.

respiratory neurons in the adult rat brainstem have the same synaptic connections as those in neonatal animals, and the same synaptic connections that are present in the adult brainstem can explain the activity patterns in the respiratory network in both neonates and adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the respiratory network is composed of a number of interacting functional modules, each of which can be examined by the methods described.
the functional connections between respiratory neurons can be determined by combining intracellular recordings and antidromic activation.
the functional connections between respiratory neurons in the adult rat medulla are consistent with the synaptic connections between neurons in other mammalian central pattern generators.
